# CDNA (CareDx, Inc.) — Technical Analysis Report
**Analysis date: 2026-10-13 | Verified close: $65.43**

## Executive Summary

CDNA has been in a powerful, event-driven uptrend since mid-July 2026, roughly doubling from ~$28.76 (2026-07-13 close) to $65.43 (2026-10-13 close). Two distinct catalysts drove the move: a gap-up on 2026-07-16 (close $40.34 vs. prior close $29.75, ~+35% single-day move on ~4.48M shares, roughly 8x normal volume) and a second acceleration phase starting 2026-09-24 (close $61.37 vs. $54.31, on ~2.5M shares). The trend remains intact — price sits well above the 50 SMA ($53.79) and 200 SMA ($30.33) — but momentum has cooled sharply in October, with a violent single-day reversal on 2026-10-06 and MACD now below its signal line. The setup is best characterized as a strong uptrend in a short-term consolidation/correction phase, with elevated volatility.

## Price Action & Trend Structure

- **Phase 1 (Jul 13 – Jul 16):** Breakout gap. From $28.76 to $40.34 in three sessions, confirmed by a massive volume expansion (561K → 4.48M shares).
- **Phase 2 (Jul 16 – Jul 29):** Post-event digestion; price drifted down to $35.41 without surrendering the gap — classic flag behavior.
- **Phase 3 (Jul 30 – Aug 27):** Renewed advance through $45–$52, interrupted by sharp pullbacks (e.g., $49.79 → $46.69 intraweek late August).
- **Phase 4 (Sep 24 – Oct 5):** Second leg higher: $54.31 → $69.85 peak close, with an intraday high of $72.51 on 2026-10-06 before a same-day collapse to a $63.79 close — a large bearish engulfing/reversal bar on the highest volume (2.56M) of the recent period.
- **Phase 5 (Oct 6 – Oct 13):** Stabilization in the $62–$65 zone. The 2026-10-13 session ($62.22 low → $65.43 close, high $67.39) shows buyers defending the low-$60s.

## Indicator Analysis

**Moving Averages — bullish alignment, wide extension.** Price ($65.43) > 10 EMA ($63.73) > 50 SMA ($53.79) > 200 SMA ($30.33). The 50 SMA is rising ~0.35/day and has not been tested since the September breakout; it now serves as the primary medium-term trend support. The extreme gap between price and the 200 SMA (>115%) confirms this is a recently re-rated stock — long-term mean reversion risk is real if the catalyst narrative fades.

**MACD — momentum rollover.** MACD line ($3.56) crossed below the signal ($4.01); histogram is negative (-0.45). MACD peaked around 2026-10-05 ($5.17) and has declined every session since, mirroring the price stall. The lines remain far above zero, so this is a momentum deceleration within an uptrend, not a confirmed trend reversal — but it argues against chasing strength here.

**RSI — cooled from extreme to neutral-bullish.** RSI hit 83.8 on 2026-10-05 (deeply overbought) and has normalized to 64.2. The reset from >80 to mid-60s while price held above $62 is constructive; there is no bearish divergence confirmed since price made its high alongside the RSI high on 10-05/10-06.

**Bollinger Bands — wide, elevated.** Bands are extremely expanded ($51.34 lower / $61.50 mid / $71.66 upper; ~$20 width), reflecting the realized volatility surge. Price at $65.43 sits in the upper half of the band, below the upper band — no overbought band tag currently. The rising lower band ($51.34) and the rising 50 SMA ($53.79) define a layered support zone in the low-to-mid $50s.

**ATR — high and rising.** ATR at $3.47 (up from ~$2.10–2.40 in August/early September) means ~5% average daily ranges. Position sizing must account for this: a 1-ATR adverse move is ~$3.50, and the 10-06 bar alone spanned $8.77 ($63.74–$72.51). Volatility has not yet contracted post-reversal, so whipsaw risk remains elevated.

## Key Levels

- **Resistance:** $67.39 (10-13 high), then $69.85–$72.51 (10-05 close / 10-06 intraday high — the reversal zone).
- **Support:** $62.20–$63.00 (10-06 to 10-12 consolidation lows, defended repeatedly including 10-13's $62.22 low), then $61.50 (Bollinger mid). Deeper: $53.79 (50 SMA) and $51.34 (lower band).
- **Volume note:** Up days in late September carried 1.7–2.5M shares; the recent pullback ran on moderating volume (~0.9–1.6M) — distribution pressure is present but not climactic.

## Actionable Insights

- **Momentum traders:** The trend is intact but the entry window for fresh longs is poor at mid-range. A pullback toward the $61.5–$63 support shelf with stabilizing volume, or a confirmed breakout above $67.4, offers better risk/reward. Use ATR-scaled stops (~$3.5+).
- **Swing traders:** Watch the MACD histogram — a re-flattening/reversal back toward zero while price holds the $62 zone would signal the correction is ending. A close below $61.5 (Bollinger mid) weakens the structure materially; below $53.8 the trend thesis is broken.
- **Risk management:** The 10-06 reversal bar is a warning that late-stage buyers were trapped at $66–$72. That overhead supply zone will likely produce selling on the first retest — treat $69.8–$72.5 as heavy resistance, not a target.
- **Caveats:** This is a single-name, catalyst-driven move; technicals describe positioning but fundamentals/news flow will dominate. All values above are from the verified snapshot; no discrepancies were found between tool outputs.

## Summary Table

| Dimension | Reading (2026-10-13) | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| Close | $65.43 | +3.7% vs. 10-12 close; holding post-reversal base |
| Trend (50/200 SMA) | $53.79 / $30.33, both rising | Strong bullish alignment; extreme extension over 200 SMA |
| 10 EMA | $63.73 | Price above; short-term momentum stabilizing |
| MACD / Signal / Hist | 3.56 / 4.01 / -0.45 | Bearish crossover — momentum cooling, not yet a trend break |
| RSI | 64.2 | Reset from 83.8 peak; neutral-bullish, no overbought flag |
| Bollinger Bands | $51.34 / $61.50 / $71.66 | Wide bands; price mid-upper half, no band tag |
| ATR | $3.47 | ~5% daily range; elevated whipsaw risk |
| Support | $62.2–$63.0, then $61.5, $53.8 | Lows repeatedly defended in low $62s |
| Resistance | $67.4, then $69.8–$72.5 | Reversal zone = heavy overhead supply |
| Volume | 1.50M (10-13) | Moderating on pullback — orderly, not climactic selling |
| Overall bias | Bullish trend, neutral short-term | Wait for pullback entry or $67.4 breakout; respect ATR-sized risk |

# CDNA (CareDx, Inc.) — Fundamental Analysis Report
**Point-in-time: 2026-10-13 | Data: SEC EDGAR filings on or before 2026-10-13, USD millions**

## Data availability caveat

Two tools returned no data for this date: `get_fundamentals` withheld profile/valuation data (vendor serves only present-day values, which would leak post-decision information), and `get_insider_transactions` was withheld (no filing-date vintage). This report is built entirely from filed financial statements. No market cap, multiples, or insider-flow read is possible within this toolset — that is a genuine coverage gap, not a neutral finding.

## Company profile

CareDx, Inc. (CDNA) is a transplant-diagnostics company — its core business is testing services and products for organ transplant patients (e.g., donor-derived cell-free DNA surveillance tests such as AlloSure/AlloMap, plus digital/transplant-center software). Revenue history in the statements is consistent with a diagnostics lab business that scaled steadily from ~$5M/quarter in 2013 to $132M in Q2 2026.

## Revenue trajectory — the standout strength

Quarterly revenue (USD M), recent trend:

| Quarter | Revenue | YoY |
|---|---|---|
| 2024-Q1 | 72 | — |
| 2024-Q2 | 92 | — |
| 2024-Q3 | 83 | — |
| 2025-Q1 | 85 | +18% |
| 2025-Q2 | 87 | -5% |
| 2025-Q3 | 100 | +20% |
| 2026-Q1 | 118 | +39% |
| 2026-Q2 | 132 | +52% |

Revenue accelerated sharply in 2026: Q1 +39% and Q2 +52% YoY, the fastest growth rates in the company's filed history. The long-run series shows roughly 10 consecutive years of growth from ~$5M to $132M/quarter.

## Profitability — an inflection, with a caveat

- **Net income**: persistent losses through 2024 (e.g., -$20M, -$23M, -$25M quarters in 2022–23; -$9M to -$11M in 2024–25). Then: Q1 2026 **+$2M**, Q2 2026 **+$3M**, and a striking **+$111M** in the latest filed quarter (column 2026-06-30), with diluted EPS of **$2.07**.
- **Operating income** shows the same pattern: -$11M (Q3 2025), -$0M, +$1M, then **+$113M** in Q2 2026.
- **Caveat**: a single-quarter +$113M operating profit on $132M revenue (86% operating margin) is far outside this company's historical economics — prior best quarters were roughly breakeven. This almost certainly includes a large one-time item (asset sale, legal settlement, impairment reversal, or similar). The same quarter shows **+$292M investing cash flow**, consistent with a major divestiture or asset monetization. Traders should treat ~breakeven-to-slightly-positive as the underlying earnings run-rate and investigate the nature of the Q2 2026 gain before capitalizing it.

## Balance sheet — strongest in company history

| Metric | 2024-12 | 2025-12 | 2026-06 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Total assets | 491 | 444 | 533 |
| Cash & equivalents | 95 | 68 | **374** |
| Current assets | 350 | 257 | 429 |
| Total liabilities | 113 | 121 | 107 |
| Stockholders equity | 379 | 311 | **426** |

Cash jumped from ~$65–78M through 2025–Q1 2026 to **$374M** at Q2 2026 — roughly half the balance sheet — driven by the ~$292M investing inflow plus positive operating cash flow. Liabilities are modest (~$107M, mostly current). Net cash position and equity (~$426M) give the company substantial financial flexibility. Equity dipped to $303M at Q1 2026 (buyback/financing outflows of -$81M in H2 2025 and -$54M in Q1 2026 suggest capital returns) before rebounding on the Q2 gain.

## Cash flow

- **Operating cash flow** turned decisively positive in 2026: +$21M (Q1) and +$35M cumulative for H1 2026, vs. -$17M for H1 2025. First sustained positive OCF since the 2020–21 period.
- **Investing**: +$292M inflow in Q2 2026 — the largest single cash event in the filing history; presumed asset sale/divestiture proceeds.
- **Financing**: -$54M (Q1 2026) and -$81M (H2 2025) — consistent with share repurchases or debt retirement.
- **Capex**: trivial (~$4–6M/quarter) — asset-light diagnostics model.

## Actionable insights for traders

1. **Bull case**: genuine operating inflection — revenue growth accelerating to +40–50% YoY *and* OCF positive *and* a fortress balance sheet ($374M cash, minimal debt). If the Q2 investing inflow was a divestiture, the remaining business is growing faster and is now self-funding.
2. **Bear/risk case**: the headline +$111M quarter is almost certainly non-recurring. Underlying earnings power is roughly breakeven-to-$3M/quarter. Valuation against one-off EPS would be a trap — but valuation tools were unavailable, so no multiple check is possible here.
3. **Must-verify before trading**: (a) what generated the +$292M investing inflow and +$113M operating income in Q2 2026 — if it's a segment sale, remaining-revenue comparability is broken; (b) whether Q3/Q4 2026 filings confirm sustained OCF.
4. **Capital returns**: heavy financing outflows suggest active buybacks — supportive for per-share value if sustained with the new cash pile.

But the retail framing is interesting: CDNA is being grouped with a hot genomics basket ($NTRA, $TXG, $MRNA), and the IBD composite 99 / RS 98 citation is quantifiable strength, not vibes. And the macro tape — yields nowhere near the ~5.9% de-risking threshold — still tolerates small-cap risk.

## Bottom line

CDNA offers what the bull market keeps paying up for: accelerating revenue (+39%/+52%), first-time profitability, $374M net cash with active capital returns, and a trend the tape has already validated twice with real catalysts. The November earnings window is the next leg's fuel. I like owning it in the low $60s with layered support at $53.8 below — risk defined, upside open.

Bear Analyst: # Bear Case — CDNA (CareDx, Inc.)

The bull just gave you a polished story about a "genuine operating inflection" and a "fortress balance sheet." Let me pull on the loose threads, because this case has a serious problem buried in its own data — and the bull actually admitted it in his own risk disclosure.

## 1. The $292M elephant in the room: did CareDx sell the crown jewels?

The fundamentals report flags — and the bull concedes — that Q2 2026 included a ~$292M investing inflow, "presumed asset sale/divestiture." The bull waves this away with "whatever the one-time item was." Whatever? That's the whole ballgame.

Think about what a ~$292M divestiture at a company this size means. Something big enough to generate that kind of cash was likely a real revenue-generating asset. If CareDx sold a business segment — say, its digital/transplant-center software arm, or a product line — then the $132M Q2 revenue and the +52% YoY growth may be the LAST print of the old company. The "remaining business growing faster" claim is an assumption, not a fact. The bull is asking you to underwrite Q3 comparability on a business mix we can't even identify from the filings cited.

And here's the tell he doesn't want you to notice: Q2's +$113M operating income on $132M revenue — an 86% operating margin — is wildly outside this company's decade of economics. If the "divestiture gain" was booked through operations, then even the headline earnings are unusable. The fundamentals report itself says treat underlying earnings as "breakeven-to-$3M/quarter." So strip the fairy dust and you're paying $65.43 — over double the July price — for a company that earns roughly $10M/year at best, on an unverified business mix.

## 2. The re-rating already happened — you're buying the aftermath

The bull says "the market has voted." Exactly — it voted months ago. CDNA went from $28.76 to $65.43 in three months. Price sits >115% above the 200 SMA. Even if every word of the bull case is true, you're not being asked to buy the inflection — you're being asked to buy it AFTER it doubled, in a consolidation phase, with momentum rolling over.

And look at what the tape is actually doing, not what the bull hopes it's doing:

- **October 6**: intraday high $72.51, same-day collapse to $63.79 — a massive bearish engulfing bar on the heaviest volume of the move (2.56M). That's not "digestion." That's a distribution event where late buyers got trapped at $66–$72. That supply is overhead now and it will sell into strength on the first retest.
- **MACD**: bearish crossover, declined every session since the 10-05 peak. The bull calls this "cooling within an uptrend" — it could just as easily be the early phase of a trend break. He won't know until $62 cracks.
- **The "defended" $62.2–$63 zone**: four touches of support isn't strength, it's a level being worn out. Every test consumes resting bids. The technical report's own line: "a close below $61.5 weakens the structure materially." The bull's entry "in the low $60s" is precisely the zone that fails if this breaks.
- **ATR $3.47, ~5% daily ranges**: this is a ~$8.77-range stock day now. Position sizing to a $3.5 ATR stop means you're risking ~5% per trade on a name that just showed it can drop $8.77 in a single session.

## 3. The sentiment "signal" is six anonymous posts and a shrug

The bull dresses up the sentiment data, but read what's actually there: six StockTwits messages, two labeled bullish, zero data from Yahoo Finance and Reddit. The most bullish post — "this baby's not slowin down" — was posted on 10-13, literally while the chart is stalling. Momentum-chasing posts clustering at local highs is a classic late-cycle tell, not confirmation. And the "sector sympathy" framing cuts against him too: if CDNA is just riding a genomics basket ($NTRA, $TXG, $MRNA), it has no idiosyncratic bid — it goes down with the basket, and it gets sold first when the sector de-grosses because it's the one that already doubled.

Meanwhile, institutional flow is pointing the other way: BlackRock turning publicly more bearish is precisely the environment where factor-driven de-grossing hits recently-doubled, thin-float mid-caps. The bull claims net cash makes CDNA "resilient" — resilient is a word for companies with earnings. A ~breakeven company trading >115% above its 200 SMA is not resilient; it's a crowded momentum trade with a cash-pile excuse.

## 4. Structural risks the bull skipped entirely

- **Reimbursement concentration**: CareDx revenue lives and dies on CMS coverage decisions for AlloSure/AlloMap and payer prior-auth friction. That's a binary, regulator-controlled revenue base — the single largest swing factor, per the macro report, and completely absent from the bull's case.
- **Historical legal overhang**: DOJ scrutiny of billing practices and short-seller reports have gapped this stock before. Nothing in the filings shown rules out the overhang returning.
- **The buyback framing**: the bull cites ~$135M of financing outflows as "capital returns." Alternative read: management bought back stock through the run-up and the Q2 equity balance still dipped to $303M before the one-time gain rescued it. If they keep spending cash defending the price into a momentum unwind, that's value destruction, not shareholder friendliness.
- **News vacuum**: no CDNA-specific news was retrievable for the whole window. The vendor gap means a pending catalyst could exist outside captured data — but a stock that doubled on "catalysts" now trading with zero confirmable news flow is a stock running on fumes.

## 5. Answering the bull directly

**"Q3 earnings is the confirmation catalyst."** Agreed — and that's the risk, not the opportunity. You want to buy a doubled stock into a November print where (a) comparability may be broken by an unexplained divestiture, (b) the prior quarter's headline EPS is unusable, and (c) any guide-down on the remaining business hits a chart sitting $30 above its 200 SMA. That's not a catalyst; that's a coin flip with a leveraged payoff asymmetry against you.

**"Buy the $61.5–$63 shelf."** That shelf is four tests old and sits on a MACD that just crossed down. If it breaks, the next real support is the 50 SMA at $53.8 — a 13% air pocket — and below that the technical report says the trend thesis itself is broken. His "defined risk" is a defined loss.

**"Yields below ~5.9% tolerate small-cap risk."** A fund-manager survey is not a rate floor. That's the softest possible evidence for macro support, and even it says positioning is comfortable — which means the marginal buyer is already in.

## Bottom line

CDNA is a ~breakeven transplant-diagnostics company whose headline numbers are contaminated by an unexplained ~$292M divestiture, trading >115% above its 200 SMA, below a fresh distribution bar, with declining momentum, trapped overhead supply at $69.8–$72.5, six-post "sentiment," and a November earnings print that could invalidate the very revenue comparability the bull case depends on. The bull's own report says verify the one-time item before sizing up — I'd extend that: don't own the stock until you know what was sold and what actually remains. Standing aside through the $61.5 support test — or shorting a failed retest of $67.4 with a stop above $72.5 — is the trade that respects both the data and the gaps in it.

Skipped: valuation multiples and insider transactions (no point-in-time data available), and the identity of the divested asset — the single biggest unknown in this entire debate. Risk you must know: the bear case leans on the Q2 gain being non-recurring and the divestiture shrinking the business; if Q3 confirms the remaining business intact and accelerating, this is a consolidation before another leg, not a top.
